newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-MIN says Mirror bid good value.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-MIN says Mirror bid good value.

text.p: Midland Independent Newspapers Plc (MIN) said on Friday that Mirror Group's 297 million stg offer for the company was fair.
"We have been talking to Mirror for some time and the price it has offered is good value for shareholders," chief executive Chris Oakley told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Mirror and MIN have agreed a price of 210 pence per share for MIN, the UK's sixth largest regional newspaper publisher and the dominant force in the area around England's second city Birmingham.

Oakley said that the MIN titles should be strengthened by a deal creating opportunities for cross-promotion, selling of advertising across regional and national titles and access to Mirror editorial resources.
Mirror has said that it expects initial cost-savings of five million stg after the deal but Oakley said that large-scale staff cuts were unlikely.
"The Mirror is not spending nearly 300 million stg to destroy the newspapers' regional identity. They will continue to require strong local editorial input."
Oakley, who is to join the Mirror's board, has a 1.5 percent stake in MIN, now worth almost 4.5 million stg.
He said he had not thought about whether to convert that into cash or whether he would take Mirror stock through a planned share alternative.
